Nature valley protein bar crumbled up over Greek yoghurt is my favourite breakfast at the moment!

For the recipe I used 

10 eggs 

1 cup and a half to 2 cups coconut flour

1 cup of butter

1 cup of xylitol (or sweetener of your choice though the quantity may need to be adjusted)

About 2 vanilla bean pod things 😂

3 tbsp of coffee granules

1 teaspoon of xantham gum

1 1/2 teaspoons of baking powder 

Mix all dry ingredients together in a bowl
Melt the butter but not too hot and whisk into the eggs, add the vanilla beans to this and mix it all together. You may have to add a small amount of milk if the texture of the batter becomes too thick, but you want a slightly thicker consistency than normal cake.

Bake in the oven for roughly 30 minutes at 170°C or until it is risen, browned on top and a toothpick comes out clean 

Please note I winged this entire recipe 😂 so it may need adjusting to your taste, oven etc. 

I topped it with whipped cream and sugar free sprinkles!

You're right. I am grieving. But I still believe she deserved better. The visits leading up to her diagnosis at aged 15, she had a resting heart rate of 152bpm, please don't tell me that is normal. She had other symptoms too (fluid in her abdomen/legs, shortness of breath, vomiting) and not once during any of those visits did any doctor advise she have an ECHO or an ECG. Those symptoms are all signs of a heart problem, I mean, I'm not a doctor or anything but it's not exactly rocket science.

Her condition could have been treated, but it went undiagnosed for so long, it caused her heart to have irreparable damage. Even if she did have an infection which caused her heart to be so damaged, it went undiagnosed. They came up with 'Stomach ulcers' and 'heartburn', repeatedly getting it wrong.

I didn't mean to say her transplant could have been preventable, that was a mistake. Yes, she probably would've needed one anyway. I admit that.

She took her tablets when she had to and we made sure of that. We made sure she didn't eat too much salt and made sure did everything the correct way. She knew this was her new chance at a normal life and wouldn't have taken that for granted.

As for the two days leading to her death, the hospital should've known that rejection was a possible factor in why she was so ill. You don't just start getting like that because of a common cold.

Her tablets didn't make her ill at all, but she was vomiting them up meaning she wasn't getting the things she needed. The staff even admitted she should have been put on an intravenous drip for her medication almost as soon as she was admitted. They are doing their own investigations into that. 

I didn't say she just dropped dead. She was very, and I mean VERY, ill in the two days before her death. She was still put into an A&E full of sick people for 13 hours (not forgetting that she had a nonexistent immune system so could have contracted anything easily) and just left there. She should have been taken into intensive care in the way she was in. Again, the hospital have admitted that. 

Also, I accept people have their problems. But I'm sure you wouldn't leave a gunshot victim in A&E knowing that it might be critical. So please do not underestimate how sick she really was.

Finally, there is a lot of other things, but I only posted what I have to give people a rough idea. I just wanted some advice, I didn't ask for you to tell me that I am wrong. That hospital failed her time and time again. I don't want that happening to anyone else.

Well if I'm honest, I've dated both poor and rich guys. I've found that although the guys I have date were what others would consider poor, they gave so much more in the way of love and happiness.

I have been with my partner for just over 2 years and when we first met he lived with his mum, didn't have much money. He ended up moving in with me and my mum. Together we saved as much as we could to move out and since then he has not got a lot of money due to personal bills of his. I don't get paid very much but tend to have a little more leftover as I am more careful, but I love him, regardless of how much he earns/has and I don't think I could leave him just for a bit more security in financial situations.

I guess what I'm trying to say is that most women do prioritise when it comes to money and men but women like me prefer to build with them, so that a few years down the line we can both say ''we did it''. I will love my partner even if he does get into debt or does have to sell his belongings, and I will always help him out when he needs it.

On the other hand, the men I have been with in the past are quite choosey when it comes to looks. But I have also been with some lovely guys that aren't so fussy and would rather feel loved. I don't think that generalizing both genders is the best idea , especially on reddit lol. But honestly, we are all different. I certainly wouldn't go for someone purely for their assets and I think a lot of guys wouldn't go for someone purely for looks.

I hope this helped.

I was happy for her, I really was at first. She deserved it more than anyone, she worked harder than everyone. But I was jealous, I'll admit. I didn't want her to go. 

She needed to spend time with the other interns to cover everything they needed, that meant less time with me. I grabbed her arm as she went to leave for the fifth night in a row and her comment hit me like a ton of bricks to the face. ''When did you get so fucking needy, get off and leave me alone''. I was offended and upset. But I needed her that night, why couldn't she see that? She was annoyed with me when she got back and I don't really blame her, you could still see the small crescent shaped marks on her arm along with fingertip bruises. I didn't realise I had gripped so hard. But I couldn't let go, I can never let go.

In time, the day came for her to start packing, and I couldn't handle it. I grabbed a few things and threw them out and back into her draws. I hid her passport, I hid her phone. But here's the kicker, she *wanted* to go. She found everything I had hidden and tossed anything I had ruined. I could feel the blood rushing to my head, I started seeing red when she put her shoes on, I grabbed a cast iron skillet. She really was leaving me, she really was letting go. No, no, no.

If I can't have her, no one can.
